summary: All 18 assertions passed. BulkChannelMessageSendJob correctly processes the subject field through parse_text with full mail-merge variable substitution. Blank/nil subjects are handled gracefully (parse_text returns '' for blank input). Duplicate detection correctly uses body-only comparison, so different subjects with the same body are still blocked.

test_details.detail: Sent bulk message to 3 candidates with subject 'Hello {{CandidateFirstName}}, opportunity at {{OrganizationName}} for {{JobTitle}}'. All 3 messages had correctly substituted subjects (e.g., 'Hello Bob, opportunity at BulkSendQAOrg for Lead QA Engineer'). No unsubstituted {{variables}} remained.

test_details.test: Test 2: All 7 mail-merge variables in subject
test_details.detail: All 7 variables (SenderFullName, SenderFirstName, JobTitle, CandidateFullName, CandidateFirstName, CandidateLastName, OrganizationName) substituted correctly in subject.
When subject is nil, parse_text returns '' (nil.blank? is true, so the early return fires). Job runs without error. Message created with empty string subject.
When subject is '', parse_text returns '' (''.blank? is true). Job runs without error. Message created with empty string subject.
Subject 'Follow up about your application' preserved unchanged through parse_text (no variables to substitute).

test_details.test: Test 6: Duplicate detection based on body, not subject
test_details.detail: Sending a message with a different subject but identical body to an existing message was correctly blocked by duplicate_message_exists? which checks body only.

test_details.test: Test 7: Non-duplicate message with different body
test_details.detail: A message with both a different subject and different body was correctly created (not blocked by duplicate detection). Subject stored correctly.

code_observations.observation: Line 14: subject is processed through parse_text identically to body (line 13). Both use the same mail-merge substitution logic.
Lines 51-66: parse_text returns '' for blank input (nil or empty string), then applies .scrub and 7 gsub substitutions for all supported variables.
Line 18: duplicate_message_exists? checks body only, not subject. This means changing only the subject does not bypass duplicate detection.
code_observations.assessment: CORRECT - this is the intended behavior since duplicate_message_exists? was designed before subject existed

code_observations.observation: Line 13: validates that body and subject do not contain unsubstituted {{variables}}. Both fields use this validator (channel_message.rb lines 24-25). If parse_text fails to substitute a variable, the record will fail validation and not be saved.
code_observations.assessment: CORRECT - provides a safety net against unsubstituted variables
